1 Peter 1.audience: Strangers far from home, who loved a Lord they had not seen, would have heard that their trials were like gold in the fire and that a living hope was kept for them in heaven.

culture.title: Strangers scattered
culture.text: The words used were legal terms for resident foreigners without full rights in the place they lived.

culture.title: Gold tried with fire
culture.text: Gold was refined by melting it so the impurities rose to the surface and could be skimmed away.

culture.title: A lamb without blemish
culture.text: Passover lambs and other sacrifices had to be without defect (Exodus 12:5; Leviticus 22:20).

1 Peter 2.audience: Believers who felt like outsiders in their cities would have heard that God called them a chosen people and a royal priesthood, and that Christ's patience under wrong was their pattern.

culture.title: Living stones
culture.text: Peter combines three stone passages: Isaiah 28:16, Psalm 118:22, and Isaiah 8:14.

culture.title: Honour the king
culture.text: The "king" was the Roman emperor. Nero ruled from AD 54 to 68.

culture.title: Household servants
culture.text: The word used means household slaves, who had no legal protection from harsh masters.

1 Peter 3.audience: Women married to unbelievers, and believers slandered by their neighbors, would have heard how a quiet spirit, a clear conscience, and a ready answer could win others and shame accusers.

culture.title: Wives and their husbands' gods
culture.text: Roman custom expected a wife to follow her husband's religion. A wife who did not could bring suspicion on the household.

culture.title: Plaiting the hair
culture.text: Elaborate braided hairstyles and gold jewelry were signs of wealth among Roman women.

culture.title: Sara called him lord
culture.text: In Genesis 18:12 Sarah refers to Abraham as "my lord."

1 Peter 4.audience: Believers whose old friends thought them strange would have heard not to be surprised at the fiery trial, to love one another, and to trust a faithful Creator.

culture.title: Abominable idolatries
culture.text: Trade guilds and city festivals held banquets honoring the gods. Refusing to attend could mean losing business and friends.

culture.title: Suffering as a Christian
culture.text: "Christian" appears only three times in the New Testament (Acts 11:26; 26:28). Around AD 112 Pliny wrote to Trajan asking how to try people accused of being Christians.

culture.title: Busybody
culture.text: The Greek word means one who meddles in other people's affairs.

1 Peter 5.audience: Church elders and younger members facing a roaring enemy would have heard to shepherd willingly, clothe themselves in humility, and cast their care on God.

culture.title: Feed the flock
culture.text: Jesus told Peter, "Feed my sheep" (John 21:16–17).

culture.title: Clothed with humility
culture.text: The Greek verb means to tie something on, and is related to a word for a worker's apron.

culture.title: A roaring lion
culture.text: Lions were known in the region and were used in Roman arenas.

2 Peter 1.audience: Believers who would soon lose their apostle would have heard Peter urge them to grow in faith and goodness, and to trust what the apostles saw and what the prophets wrote.

culture.title: Putting off this tabernacle
culture.text: Peter calls his body a tent. Tradition says Peter was crucified in Rome under Nero.

culture.title: Eyewitnesses
culture.text: Peter recalls being with Jesus "in the holy mount" at the transfiguration (Matthew 17:1–5).

culture.title: Cunningly devised fables
culture.text: Greek writers used the word myth for stories about the gods.

2 Peter 2.audience: Believers surrounded by smooth teachers who loved gain would have heard that God judges false teachers and still knows how to rescue the godly.

culture.title: Tartarus
culture.text: "Cast them down to hell" translates a verb based on Tartarus, the deepest part of the underworld in Greek myth.

culture.title: Balaam's ass
culture.text: Balaam was rebuked by his donkey on the way to curse Israel for pay (Numbers 22:21–35).

culture.title: The dog and the sow
culture.text: The first proverb is Proverbs 26:11; the second was a known saying.

2 Peter 3.audience: Believers mocked for waiting on the Lord's return would have heard that his delay is longsuffering, and that they were to live holy lives while they looked for a new heaven and earth.

culture.title: A thousand years as one day
culture.text: The wording echoes Psalm 90:4.

culture.title: Elements melting
culture.text: Stoic philosophers taught that the universe would end in fire and be renewed.

culture.title: Paul's epistles
culture.text: This is one of the earliest references to a collection of Paul's letters, and it places them alongside "the other scriptures."

1 John 1.audience: Believers unsettled by teachers who had left them would have heard firsthand witnesses say that the Word of life was seen and touched, and that God is light.

culture.title: Walking in the light
culture.text: The Dead Sea Scrolls also contrast the sons of light and the sons of darkness.

culture.title: Fellowship
culture.text: The Greek word koinonia means sharing in common, and was also used of business partnerships (Luke 5:10).

1 John 2.audience: A church hurt by those who had gone out would have heard Christ named as advocate, and that loving the brethren and not the world marks those who abide in him.

culture.title: An advocate
culture.text: The Greek word paraclete means one called alongside to help, such as a legal advocate. John uses it for the Holy Spirit in John 14:16.

culture.title: Antichrist
culture.text: The word appears in the Bible only in 1 and 2 John (1 John 2:18, 22; 4:3; 2 John 1:7).

culture.title: An unction
culture.text: Anointing with oil marked kings and priests for their office (1 Samuel 16:13; Exodus 29:7).

1 John 3.audience: Believers doubting their standing would have heard that they are already God's children, that Christ laid down his life, and that real love acts in deed and in truth.

culture.title: Cain
culture.text: Cain killed his brother Abel after God accepted Abel's offering (Genesis 4:3–8).

culture.title: This world's good
culture.text: The Greek word bios means livelihood or the means of living.

1 John 4.audience: A church pressed by false prophets would have heard to try the spirits, and that God's love in sending his Son is the pattern for loving one another.

culture.title: Come in the flesh
culture.text: Later, some teachers called Docetists claimed that Jesus only seemed to have a human body. Ignatius of Antioch wrote against this view around AD 110.

culture.title: Testing prophets
culture.text: The law also taught how to recognize a false prophet (Deuteronomy 13:1–5; 18:21–22).

1 John 5.audience: Believers wanting certainty would have heard that faith in the Son overcomes the world, that eternal life is theirs, and that they may ask God with confidence.

culture.title: Water and blood
culture.text: John's Gospel records water and blood flowing from Jesus' side at the cross (John 19:34).

culture.title: The three that bear record in heaven
culture.text: The words "in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost" in verses 7–8 are not found in early Greek manuscripts.

culture.title: Idols
culture.text: Images of gods stood in temples, homes, and public places throughout Greek and Roman cities.

2 John 1.audience: A house church that welcomed travelling teachers would have heard to keep their love joined to the truth about Christ, and to refuse hospitality to those who denied it.

culture.title: Receive him not into your house
culture.text: Traveling teachers depended on believers' hospitality for lodging and support.

culture.title: Paper and ink
culture.text: Letters were written with ink made from soot and gum on papyrus sheets. A single sheet held a short letter like this one.

3 John 1.audience: A host who opened his home to travelling believers would have heard the elder's thanks, and a church under a leader who loved first place would have heard what to follow and what to refuse.

culture.title: Bringing them forward on their journey
culture.text: Hosts provided travelers with food, money, and supplies for the next stage of the trip (Titus 3:13).

culture.title: Taking nothing of the Gentiles
culture.text: Traveling teachers who refused payment from outsiders depended on believers' support.

culture.title: Pen and ink
culture.text: Pens were cut from reeds.

Jude 1.audience: Believers whose church had been quietly infiltrated would have heard a plain warning with old examples, and a call to stay in the love of God and rescue the wavering.

culture.title: Michael and the body of Moses
culture.text: This dispute is not in the Old Testament. Early Christian writers said it came from a book called The Assumption of Moses.

culture.title: Enoch prophesied
culture.text: Jude quotes 1 Enoch 1:9, a Jewish writing well known at the time; copies were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls.

culture.title: Feasts of charity
culture.text: Early believers shared common meals, called love feasts (agape).
